capacity: 56,000. This figure is unusually stable and is stated by multiple sources. (a) Ballparks of Baseball, https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/dodger-stadium/ — verbatim: '-Capacity: 56,000'. The same page notes the capacity has been deliberately held at that number through every renovation: 'These updates added roughly 1,500 seats but maintained the stadium's official capacity at 56,000' and 'Additional seating and restrooms were added to the bleacher pavilions, but the stadium's capacity remains 56,000.' (b) Web search of SABR (https://sabr.org/journal/article/dodger-stadium-exactly-56000-seats/) and MLB.com's own Dodger Stadium guide: 'For over six decades, the Dodgers have maintained that the capacity of their stadium is exactly 56,000, despite a number of renovations over the years' and 'Dodger Stadium is the biggest MLB stadium by capacity (56,000).' The 56,000 number is reportedly tied to the city conditional-use permit (16,000 parking spaces x 3.5 people). RECOMMENDED: 56,000. No conflicting figure was found. CAVEAT: the SABR article title 'Dodger Stadium: Exactly 56,000 Seats?' implies the real physical seat count differs from the published figure; the actual seat count was NOT established — UNKNOWN. Original 1962 opening-day attendance cited by Ballparks of Baseball was 'over 52,000'. The Wikipedia article was not fetched directly in this session.

numbering_direction.summary: DODGER STADIUM DOES NOT USE A SINGLE INCREASING SWEEP. Section numbers START AT HOME PLATE AND INCREASE OUTWARD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE, SPLIT BY PARITY: ODD-NUMBERED SECTIONS RUN DOWN THE THIRD BASE SIDE (toward LEFT field); EVEN-NUMBERED SECTIONS RUN DOWN THE FIRST BASE SIDE (toward RIGHT field). Within each side, the number INCREASES as you move away from home plate toward the foul pole and then into the outfield. On a chart drawn with home plate at the bottom, the odd series runs anti-clockwise (to the left) and the even series runs clockwise (to the right), and each series is a mirror of the other: sections N and N+1 are the same distance from home plate on opposite sides. This parity rule holds on EVERY level. LEVEL BY LEVEL: (a) FIELD LEVEL 1-53 — 1 (odd, 3B side) and 2 (even, 1B side) flank home plate; 1-25 is the infield; 15,17,19,21,23,25,27 sit behind the Dodgers dugout (3B side); 14,16,18,20,22,24,26 sit behind the visiting dugout (1B side); 26-53 run down the baselines to the corners; 46-52 (even) are the right-field line; 53 (odd, highest) is the far LEFT-field corner next to the Dodgers bullpen; 52 (even, highest) is the far RIGHT-field corner. (b) LOGE LEVEL 101-168 — 101 (odd, 3B) and 102 (even, 1B) are directly behind home plate; odd 123-165 is the third base line; 152 (even) and 153 (odd) are a symmetric pair of restroom locations; 167 (odd) sits by the Dodgers bullpen in left field, 168 (even) by the visitors bullpen in right field. (c) CLUB / SUITE LEVEL — private suites 201LS-233LS occupy behind home plate and the right field side; the ticketed Executive Club sections 229-261 (ODD ONLY) run from shallow LEFT field out to the LEFT field foul pole. (d) RESERVE LEVEL 1-61 — Infield Reserve 1-11 is between the dugouts and behind home plate; odd runs to third base, even to first base; Reserve 30 (even) is 'down the right-field line'; restrooms at Reserve 31 (odd, 3B) and 32 (even, 1B) are again a symmetric pair. (e) TOP DECK 1TD-13TD — 1TD-3TD directly behind home plate, numbers rising toward the baselines; the Top Deck spans only first base to third base. (f) PAVILION 301-316 — ODD 301-315 is the LEFT FIELD Pavilion (Spectrum Pavilion), EVEN 302-316 is the RIGHT FIELD Pavilion (Coca-Cola Pavilion); within each, 301/302 are the innermost (nearest the foul lines and the bullpens) and 315/316 the outermost toward centre field. (g) DUGOUT CLUB 1DC-15DC — 1DC-5DC and 7DC behind home plate; ODD 9DC,11DC,13DC,15DC behind the DODGERS dugout; EVEN 6DC,8DC,10DC behind the VISITING dugout (RateYourSeats mislabels which physical side these are on — see the 'uncertain' list — but the parity assignment matches every other source). THE SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING CONFIRMATION IS THE OFFICIAL DODGERS NETTING STATEMENT, which names one section on each side by number and by side.

levels.name: Top Deck (uppermost level; suffix 'TD')
levels.notes: Verbatim: 'Highest Seats in the Stadium: The Top Deck is the uppermost level on the Dodger Stadium seating chart.' 'The Top Deck is the highest seating level at Dodger Stadium, located above all other tiers and positioned primarily behind home plate. These sections are labeled 1TD-13TD on the Dodgers seating chart.' 'Sections 1TD-3TD sit directly behind home plate and are generally considered the most desirable seats on this level thanks to their centered location. As sections extend toward the baselines, the viewing angle becomes more extreme.' 'Very Steep Seating: Steep aisles help maintain clear sightlines but require climbing many stairs.' 'Limited Shade: Most seats are exposed to the Southern California sun with minimal overhead coverage.' 'Most seats in the Top Deck are fully exposed during day games, and the only potential shade is typically found in the last couple rows, where a small roof above may provide limited relief.' Corroborating from Ballparks of Baseball: 'a five-tier seating structure that stretches from the left-field foul pole to home plate and around to the right-field foul pole, with the exception of the uppermost deck, which spans from first base to third base.' Row range per Top Deck section was NOT established — UNKNOWN (an RYS photo filename references 'Section 9TD Row H'). NOTE: the RYS section index shows the DISPLAY LABEL for section 1TD as 'Top Deck 1T' (apparent RYS data typo); the URL id is '1TD'.

levels.name: Pavilion (outfield bleachers)
levels.sections: 301-316. ODD 301-315 = Left Field Pavilion (Spectrum Pavilion). EVEN 302-316 = Right Field Pavilion (Coca-Cola Pavilion).
levels.notes: Verbatim: 'Outfield Bleacher Seating: Pavilion sections are located beyond the outfield wall in left and right field.' 'Bleacher-Style Seating: Continuous bench seating with a backrest instead of individual stadium chairs.' 'Seating in these sections is bleacher-style, featuring a single continuous bench in each row. Unlike traditional bleachers, the benches include a backrest.' 'Pavilion sections extend deep into the outfield with rows labeled A through V.' 'The Dodgers bullpen is closest to section 301.' 'Because this side of the stadium sits on the east side, these seats [Right Field Pavilion] typically receive the most sun exposure at Dodger Stadium, especially during afternoon games.' 'In previous seasons, these sections were part of the All-You-Can-Eat Pavilion seating experience. That offering was discontinued following the Dodger Stadium renovations completed before the 2020 season, and the sections now function as standard pavilion seating.' ROW CONFLICT: the zone page says rows 'A through V' but the Section 301 page says 'Rows in Section 301 are labeled A-X' with 'Entrances to this section are located at Rows A and N' — see 'uncertain'. An RYS photo caption adds: 'The highest rows of seating in the outfield pavilion are covered.' Section 301 page: 'Rows T and above are under cover.'

levels.name: Home Run Seats (in front of the Pavilion, both outfield corners)
levels.sections: Left Home Run Seats A-D and Right Home Run Seats A-D (8 labels in the RYS index; no individual RYS section pages)
levels.notes: Verbatim: 'Closest Seats to the Outfield Wall: Two-row seating sections located directly in front of the Outfield Pavilion.' 'Unique Bar-Style Seating: Fans sit on padded bar stools along a drink rail rather than traditional stadium seats.' 'The seating area consists of two rows of bar-style seating, positioned right along the field-facing drink rail.' 'Sections in this area are labeled A-D, with each section designated for either Left Field or Right Field depending on its location in the outfield.' 'This placement makes them the closest seats the ballpark has ever had to the outfield wall.' All-inclusive food and non-alcoholic beverages plus in-seat wait service for Dodgers games. Whether the two rows are labelled with numbers or letters is UNKNOWN.

dugouts.home: THIRD BASE side. Dodger Stadium is one of the minority of MLB parks where the home dugout is NOT on the first base side. The Dodgers dugout fronts the ODD-numbered sections; RateYourSeats names odd Field Level sections 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27 and odd Dugout Club sections 9DC, 11DC, 13DC, 15DC as the sections behind it.
dugouts.visiting: FIRST BASE side, fronting the EVEN-numbered sections; RateYourSeats names even Field Level sections 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 and even Dugout Club sections 6DC, 8DC, 10DC as the sections behind it.
dugouts.source: PRIMARY (independent of RateYourSeats): https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/dodger-stadium/ — verbatim in the Facts & Figures block: '-Home Dugout: Third Base'. CORROBORATION 1 (parity + team, RYS Field Level review reproduced on every field-level section page, e.g. https://www.rateyourseats.com/uniqlo-field-at-dodger-stadium/seating/sections/1): 'Fans hoping to sit near the Dodgers dugout should look toward odd-numbered sections 15–27, while visiting fans hoping to sit near their team's dugout should consider even-numbered sections 14–26.' CORROBORATION 2 (ties odd sections behind the Dodgers dugout explicitly to the third base side): https://www.rateyourseats.com/uniqlo-field-at-dodger-stadium/seating/shaded-covered-seats — 'search for tickets in the back rows (N and higher) of the odd numbered Field Level Sections behind the Dodgers dugout (Sections 15-27, odd numbers only)' in a passage whose whole point is that the third base side gets the shade. CORROBORATION 3 (official, fixes odd = third base): https://www.mlb.com/dodgers/ballpark/netting — 'baseline section 40 (first base side) and baseline section 41 (third base side)'. CORROBORATION 4 (home bullpen in left field, i.e. the third base side): see 'bullpens'. CONTRADICTION — DO NOT TRUST: https://www.rateyourseats.com/uniqlo-field-at-dodger-stadium/seating/dugout-club states the exact opposite sides: 'Sections 6DC, 8DC, and 10DC are positioned along the third base side behind the visiting team dugout' and 'Sections 9DC, 11DC, 13DC, and 15DC are located along the first base side behind the Dodgers dugout.' This is the single-guide inversion warned about; five independent sources including two official Dodgers pages and Ballparks of Baseball say the Dodgers dugout is on the THIRD base side.

bullpens: BOTH BULLPENS ARE BEYOND THE OUTFIELD WALL, in front of / below the Pavilion sections, one in left field and one in right field. DODGERS (HOME) BULLPEN = LEFT FIELD (third base side, odd sections). RateYourSeats Pavilion page, verbatim: 'The Dodgers bullpen is closest to section 301, giving fans in this area a close look at relief pitchers warming up throughout the game.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/uniqlo-field-at-dodger-stadium/seating/pavilion-seats). Fan feedback on Section 53 (field level, far left field corner), verbatim: 'Section 53 is right next to the Dodgers bullpen.' and 'The Dodgers Bullpen is to the Left of Section 53 — Sit in a higher number seat (8-10) in Section 53 to be close to the Dodgers bullpen.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/uniqlo-field-at-dodger-stadium/seating/sections/53). Fan feedback on Section 301, verbatim: 'The Dodger Bullpen is near Section 301.' and 'The Dodgers Bullpen is to the Right of Section 301 — Sit in a higher number seat (8 or 9) in Section 301 to be close to the Dodgers bullpen.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/uniqlo-field-at-dodger-stadium/seating/sections/301). VISITING BULLPEN = RIGHT FIELD (first base side, even sections). Web-search summary of aviewfrommyseat / tickpick / RYS content states the Dodgers bullpen sits 'between sections 53, 167, and 301' and 'The visitors' bullpen is in front of sections 52, 168, and 302' — that even/odd mirror is exactly what the parity rule predicts, but NO primary URL was fetched for the visiting-bullpen section numbers, so treat '52 / 168 / 302' as single-sourced. BULLPEN OVERLOOKS: Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: 'In 2014, bullpen overlooks were added, providing fans with seating and lounging areas overlooking the action in the bullpens.' A web-search summary of RYS's bullpen-overlook blog post adds: 'Behind each bullpen in left and right field will be an elevated area where fans can hang out and get an up-close look down into the bullpen.' There is also a 'Right Field Bar & Bullpen Overlook' venue listed publicly at 1000 Elysian Park Ave. The ticketed section identifiers for the bullpen overlooks are UNKNOWN and none appear in the RYS section index. MINOR INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the Section 301 fan feedback says the bullpen is 'to the Right of Section 301' yet advises sitting in HIGHER seat numbers, whereas RYS's own seat-1 rule puts higher numbers on the LEFT when facing the field; the equivalent Section 53 feedback ('to the Left ... higher number seat') is self-consistent. Flagged in 'uncertain'.

accessibility.summary: Accessible seating is available on EVERY level of Dodger Stadium. Official Dodgers text, verbatim: 'Accessible Seating — Accessible seating is available on every level of the stadium. Guests may purchase tickets for accessible seating by clicking the "ADA Tickets" link at several places on our website, or by selecting "accessiblilty" on the right of any ticket selection wepbage. Guests may also contact the Dodgers' ticket office by calling 866-DODGERS ext. 8 with any specific ADA seating requirements.' [sic — the typos are in the source.] ELEVATORS/ESCALATORS, verbatim: 'The stadium has 9 elevators.' 'Three elevators are located behind homeplate, two of which access all levels, while the third travels between levels 5 & 7. Two elevators located at either end of the concourses access levels 2 through 7, and one elevator, located in Center Field, accesses all three levels of the pavilions. The Dugout Club features an elevator for the convenience of guests unable to take the stairs into the Dugout Club Lounge and seats.' 'The stadium has two sets of escalators located behind Homeplate which travel between levels 2 (Field Level), 4 (Loge Level), and 5 (Suite Level).' 'There are escalators which travel between Loge and Reserve on both sides of the stadium near the entry gates.' 'There are escalators that travel from Reserve to Top Deck near the entry gates.' [This also names the level numbering: level 2 = Field, level 4 = Loge, level 5 = Suite, and levels run to 7.] WHEELCHAIR STORAGE/ESCORTS, verbatim: 'Guests using wheelchairs who prefer to sit in standard seating may check in and store their wheelchair or other mobility device by bringing them to designated areas on the Left and Right Field plazas on Field level, adjacent to the Fan Services Stations, or behind home plate on all other levels. Escorts for those requiring wheelchair assistance are available inside the stadium from any gate on a first-come, first served basis by contacting any Security, Guest Services, or Fan Services team members.' PARKING, verbatim: 'The accessible parking spaces required by law are located in parking lots B, D, G, I, L, N, & P.' SHUTTLE, verbatim: 'The Los Angeles Dodgers offer a courtesy shuttle that is reserved for our guests seeking mobility assistance. This shuttle operates from the various parking lots to the areas near the entry gates. In order to arrange for this service once you have parked, you may call the Dodger Hotline at (323) 224-2611.' OTHER: assistive listening devices at any Fan Services Station; closed captioning via the MLB Ballpark app; sensory bags at any Fan Services Station and a sensory room on the first level of the Right Field Pavilion; an adult changing table inside the All-Gender Restroom at Section 32 on the Reserve Level; accessibility device charging outlets at select accessible seating locations (MVP@ladodgers.com or 866-DODGERS ext. 8); service animals welcome (emotional support animals prohibited); mobility devices may not be left unattended. RateYourSeats adds a photo caption: 'Accessible seating spaces are available at the top of some loge level sections. Companions are seated on a traditional stadium chair with a cupholder.' NOTE: https://www.mlb.com/dodgers/ballpark/accessibility returned an EMPTY body; all official text above comes from https://www.mlb.com/dodgers/ballpark/information/guide, which was fetched in full and read section by section.
landmarks: Three elevators behind home plate (two serve all levels; the third serves levels 5-7) — the most important accessible vertical circulation point and an independent confirmation that the bowl is centred on home plate
Two elevators at either end of the concourses serving levels 2 through 7
One elevator in Center Field serving all three levels of the pavilions
Dugout Club elevator (into the Dugout Club Lounge and seats)
Two sets of escalators behind home plate serving level 2 (Field), level 4 (Loge) and level 5 (Suite)
Escalators between Loge and Reserve on BOTH sides of the stadium near the entry gates (symmetric pair)
Escalators from Reserve to Top Deck near the entry gates

All-Gender / wheelchair-accessible single-stall restrooms: Loge Level Sections 152 and 153; Reserve Level Sections 31 and 32; Suite Level across from Suite 211 and the Champions Lounge; Top Deck between the Top of The Park store and the restrooms; Center Field Left Pavilion and Right Pavilion. NONE on Field Level — 'Field Level – None on this level. Please refer to left and right pavilions or Loge level.'
Adult changing table inside the All-Gender Restroom at Section 32, Reserve Level
Wheelchair check-in/storage: Left and Right Field plazas on Field level adjacent to the Fan Services Stations; behind home plate on all other levels
Accessible parking lots B, D, G, I, L, N and P
Courtesy mobility shuttle from the parking lots to the entry gates — Dodger Hotline (323) 224-2611
Sensory room on the first level of the Right Field Pavilion
Go-Ahead Entry participating gates: Left Centerfield; Left Field, Field Level; Right Field, Field Level; Left Field, Loge Level
Contacts: Fan Services 866-DODGERS ext. 7; accessible ticketing 866-DODGERS ext. 8; Dodger Hotline 323-224-2611 or text LADFAN to 69050
FULL GATE NAME LIST — UNKNOWN. Only the Go-Ahead Entry gates and 'Sunset Gate A on Vin Scully Ave' and 'Gate B' (rideshare, Lot 1) were named in the sources fetched.

row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE LETTERED ALMOST EVERYWHERE AT DODGER STADIUM, not numbered — this park is the opposite of the numbered-row parks earlier in this project. CONFIRMED PER-SECTION ROW LABELS from RateYourSeats section pages: Section 1 — 'Rows in Section 1 are labeled A-X, DR'; Section 2 — 'Rows in Section 2 are labeled A-X, DR'; Section 53 — 'Rows in Section 53 are labeled AA, A-Z'; Section 301 — 'Rows in Section 301 are labeled A-X'. PER-LEVEL ROW CONVENTIONS: (a) Field Level — letters A onward, with an extra leading row 'AA' in at least some outfield-corner sections (53) and an extra trailing row 'DR' in at least the home-plate sections (1, 2); 'DR' is almost certainly the drink-rail / rail-seating row, because the same pages say 'There is rail seating behind Row X'. (b) Pavilion — 'rows labeled A through V' per the zone page, but 'A-X' per the Section 301 page (conflict). (c) Reserve Level, Lower Reserve/Infield Reserve — 'Rows are labeled A through V, with Row A located at the bottom of the section closest to the field'; sold as VIP (Rows A-H) and MVP (Rows J-V); note row I is skipped. (d) Reserve Level, Value Reserve — 'Rows in these sections are labeled with double letters, starting with Row AA at the front near the concourse tunnels', roughly 9 rows, and 'Row DD is the fourth row in the section' (so AA, BB, CC, DD, ...). (e) Loge Level — lettered (RYS references 'Rows N and higher', and photo filenames show Row R and Row T); the per-section range was NOT established — UNKNOWN. (f) Top Deck — lettered (photo filename 'Section 9TD Row H'); range UNKNOWN. (g) Dugout Club — 'All Dugout Club seats are located within the first nine rows of the field'; an RYS photo is captioned 'dugout club 8, row dd', implying doubled letters are used here too; the actual range is UNKNOWN. (h) Baseline Club — quoted as NUMBERED 'Rows 1-6 of sections 26-43', which conflicts with the lettered rows shown on the same sections' pages — see 'uncertain'. ENTRANCE-ROW BEHAVIOUR: entrances are generally at the BACK/TOP of the section, because fans enter from a concourse behind and walk down. Verbatim examples: Section 1 and Section 2 — 'An entrance to this section is located at Row X' (the last lettered row); Section 53 — 'An entrance to this section is located at Row Z'; Reserve Level — 'All sections on this level share a single concourse, where fans enter from the back of the section and walk down toward their seats' and 'fans will enter near Row V and walk down toward their seats'. EXCEPTION: Section 301 (Left Field Pavilion) — 'Entrances to this section are located at Rows A and N', i.e. two entrances, one at the very front. SEAT NUMBERING: seat 1 is on the RIGHT when facing the field on every page checked (see seat1_side_verbatim), i.e. seat numbers increase toward the viewer's LEFT. Field-level rows are short — 'Most rows contain no more than eight seats' — and fan tips reference 'seat (8-10)' and 'seat (8 or 9)' as the high end. ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL CONVENTION (WC / WCH / VWC / AC suffix or similar) — UNKNOWN. No source consulted used any such label. The Dodgers say only that 'Accessible seating is available on every level of the stadium', and RateYourSeats describes accessible positions positionally: 'Accessible seating spaces are available at the top of some loge level sections. Companions are seated on a traditional stadium chair with a cupholder.' The 'DR' row label observed on Field Level sections 1 and 2 is rail seating, NOT an accessible-row label.
seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the right" — quoted verbatim from the 'Row Numbers' block of RateYourSeats section pages at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. The sentence is IDENTICAL, word for word, on every section page fetched: https://www.rateyourseats.com/uniqlo-field-at-dodger-stadium/seating/sections/1 (Field Level, behind home plate, third base side of the plate), /sections/2 (Field Level, behind home plate, first base side of the plate), /sections/53 (Field Level, far left field corner, third base side) and /sections/301 (Left Field Pavilion, beyond the outfield wall). These span two different levels, both parities, the infield and the outfield, so the rule appears to be park-wide: seat 1 is on the RIGHT as you face the field, and seat numbers increase toward your LEFT. NOTE the exact wording differs slightly from the phrasing used at some other parks in this project ('When looking towards the stage/field' vs 'When looking towards the field/stage') — the Dodger Stadium pages all say 'field/stage'. NO CONTRADICTING STATEMENT was found. NOT independently verified for the Loge Level (101-168), the Suite/Club Level (201LS-233LS, 229-261), the Reserve Level (IR/LR/R) or the Top Deck (1TD-13TD) — no section page on those levels was individually fetched in this session. PARTIAL CORROBORATION from fan feedback, and one partial contradiction: Section 53 — 'The Dodgers Bullpen is to the Left of Section 53 — Sit in a higher number seat (8-10) in Section 53 to be close to the Dodgers bullpen' (CONSISTENT: higher numbers are on the left). Section 301 — 'The Dodgers Bullpen is to the Right of Section 301 — Sit in a higher number seat (8 or 9) in Section 301 to be close to the Dodgers bullpen' (INCONSISTENT with the rule; if higher numbers are on the left, the advice and the direction disagree). These are unmoderated fan comments, not the RYS rule block.
known_obstructions: PROTECTIVE NETTING — PREFER THE OFFICIAL DODGERS LIST. https://www.mlb.com/dodgers/ballpark/netting, verbatim in full: 'The Dodgers have protective netting which extends from behind home plate to the end of baseline section 40 (first base side) and baseline section 41 (third base side). The coverage of netting or screening will vary by section. Fans are still exposed to objects leaving the field of play, including bats and bat fragments, and thrown or batted balls; ticket holder assumes all risk of injury. For more information on netting or screening coverage and seating options, please contact the Los Angeles Dodgers ticket office at (866) DODGERS, Extension 7.' So the netting covers Field Level sections 1 through 41 (odd side) / 1 through 40 (even side) — i.e. essentially everything from home plate out to the end of the baseline sections on both sides. CONFLICTING (narrower) CLAIM: RateYourSeats fan feedback, repeated on sections 1, 2 and the shaded-seats page, says 'Front of sections 1-25 are behind the netting — There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 1-25. The height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section.' RECOMMENDED: use the official 40/41 extent; the RYS 1-25 range is stale or refers only to the infield portion. The Dugout Club page adds: 'Protective netting is present in these areas for safety, but most fans quickly forget it's there due to how close the action feels.' OVERHANGS / STRUCTURAL OBSTRUCTION: the biggest documented obstruction at Dodger Stadium is the deck overhang cutting off the view of the videoboards and of high fly balls from the back rows. RYS venue photo caption, verbatim: 'The view from the last row in section 5 at Dodger Stadium. Notice how the overhang will obstruct views of the videoboards and flyballs.' Another, on the Loge bar tops: 'The view from the bar tops behind the loge level. The overhang is a little obstructive.' A fan comment adds: 'The upper deck overhang is among the smallest in baseball, especially down the first base line.' VIDEOBOARDS: Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: 'Another distinctive feature is the pair of jumbo hexagonal HD video scoreboards located behind the bleachers in left and right field' — so there is no centre-field board, and the boards themselves are what the overhang hides from the back rows. CONCERT-ONLY OBSTRUCTION: the Section 301 page carries an explicit warning: '301 is behind the stage or to the side of the stage for most concerts. This may restrict or limit your view of the performance.' SUN (not an obstruction but the dominant comfort factor here): the Right Field Pavilion 'sits on the east side' and receives the most sun; 'Field level sections 46-52, and nearly all the Reserve level sections on the first base side will have the sun directly in your eyes at first pitch'; the shaded options are the back rows of the odd/third-base Loge sections 123-165, the Executive Club (almost completely covered), Infield Reserve 1-11 rows M and above, and the highest Top Deck rows. COVER RANGES quoted per section: sections 1, 2, 53 and 301 — 'Rows T and above are under cover'; a photo caption instead says 'The loge level protects rows K and above on the field level' (conflict, see 'uncertain'). NO pole or railing obstruction reports were found for any section. NO source states whether the netting is a knotless/thin type.
uncertain: VENUE NAME FORM: the field is now 'UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium' (2026, five-year UNIQLO deal), but the BUILDING is still 'Dodger Stadium' and MLB's own article stresses the old name 'isn't going away'. Decide deliberately which form the generated copy uses. Capitalisation is inconsistent across sources: MLB and the Dodgers write 'UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium'; RateYourSeats writes 'Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium'. Ballparks of Baseball is STALE and still says '-Former Name(s): None' and '-Naming Rights: None'. RateYourSeats' internal master_id is still 'dodger-stadium-los-angeles-ca' and its images are still 'dodger-stadium-*.jpg' — legacy strings, not current names.

DUGOUT SIDE — RESOLVED BUT WITH A DIRECT SOURCE CONFLICT ON RECORD. RateYourSeats' Dugout Club page says 'Sections 9DC, 11DC, 13DC, and 15DC are located along the first base side behind the Dodgers dugout' and '6DC, 8DC, and 10DC are positioned along the third base side behind the visiting team dugout'. This is INVERTED relative to Ballparks of Baseball ('-Home Dugout: Third Base'), the official Dodgers netting page (section 41 = third base side, and odd sections are the Dodgers side per RYS's own Field Level review), RYS's own shaded-seats page ('the odd numbered Field Level Sections behind the Dodgers dugout (Sections 15-27, odd numbers only)' in a passage about the third base side getting shade), and the bullpen geography (Dodgers bullpen in LEFT field). Recommended: Dodgers dugout = THIRD BASE. Do not use the Dugout Club page's side labels.

SECTION-ID SUFFIXES: RateYourSeats strips the official Dodgers level suffixes for some levels and invents its own for others. Official Dodgers ticket designations appear to be FD (Field), LG (Loge), RS (Reserve), TD (Top Deck), DC (Dugout Club) — RYS's own expert answer says 'Section 30RS, or Reserve 30'. But the RYS index uses bare numbers for Field (1-53), Loge (101-168), Executive Club (229-261) and Pavilion (301-316), and uses IR / LR / R (its own Infield Reserve / Lower Reserve / Value Reserve zone tags) instead of RS on the Reserve Level, and LS for suites. The 'sections' array above records the RYS identifiers exactly as they appear in the index. RECONCILE AGAINST THE OFFICIAL DODGERS SEATING CHART BEFORE PUBLISHING — this is the biggest remaining risk in this file.

NUMBER COLLISIONS ACROSS LEVELS: bare numbers 1-53 (Field) collide with Reserve 1-61 and Dugout Club 1-15 and Top Deck 1-13; bare numbers 229-261 (Executive Club) collide with suite numbers 229LS-233LS on the SAME level. Any lookup keyed on the bare number alone will be ambiguous. RYS disambiguates only via the URL suffix.

BASELINE CLUB ROW LABELS: the Field Level review says 'Rows 1-6 of sections 26-43 are part of the premium Baseline Club' — NUMBERED rows — while every field-level section page fetched shows LETTERED rows (A-X, or AA plus A-Z). Either the Baseline Club really does use numbered rows 1-6 in front of the lettered rows, or RYS is paraphrasing 'the first six rows'. UNRESOLVED. Also note the Baseline Club range 26-43 spans BOTH parities, i.e. both baselines.
PAVILION ROW RANGE: zone page says 'rows labeled A through V' (twice, once for each pavilion); the Section 301 page says 'Rows in Section 301 are labeled A-X'. Conflict of two rows. Unresolved.

FIELD LEVEL COVER LINE: section pages 1, 2 and 53 say 'Rows T and above are under cover'; an RYS venue photo caption says 'The loge level protects rows K and above on the field level.' Conflict. The per-section statement is probably the more reliable.

NETTING EXTENT: official Dodgers page says the net runs to sections 40 (1B) and 41 (3B); RateYourSeats fan feedback says only 'sections 1-25'. Use the official figure and flag the discrepancy. Neither source says whether the net reaches the foul poles (it explicitly does not — it ends at the end of the baseline sections).

ORIENTATION: no source consulted gives a compass bearing for home plate or center field. The only literal statement is that the Right Field Pavilion 'sits on the east side' of the stadium. 'Batter faces northeast' is an inference from that plus the sun/shade behaviour. Verify against a mapping source before publishing any compass claim.
